coverage: The reasoning of the worker. Only actions, outputs and reports are seen.
Whether a tool did what it reported.
Events that never reached a hook.
A tool call that another installed mod answered before the hooks ran. The receipt lists the plugins and mods loaded at session start, so a reader can see what else was present.
Actions taken outside Claude Code on the same machine.
Correctness that no charter check expresses.
Any effect in an outside system beyond the fact that a call was made.
A change to columns of the source table that no check reads. A shell command that the allow list permits can rewrite them, and the demo checks see emails and counts only (D-062).
A worker that skips its own validation. The daemon runs the exit checks itself, so nothing is flagged when the result is good (D-062).
The order of stages. A skipped or reordered stage with no report raises no flag from the checks (D-062).
A stage report that cites a check result the ledger does not show. No cross-check is built. A bad result is still caught by the exit check (D-062).

A criterion with no check, such as the one about the most recent contact details in the demo. The demo answer key was extended to cover contact details after the first run showed that the first key missed F19 (D-065), so catching F19 shows that the key can catch what it was written for, not that a key written without knowing the failure would. A wrong result on a criterion that neither a check nor the key covers is only left not verified.
limits: This receipt gives evidence about a run. It makes no claim beyond what the checks that ran and the ledger show.

The ledger is tamper-evident on one machine, not tamper-proof. The anchors are kept outside the run folder, on the same machine, under the same user. The git anchor is not built, so there is no anchor outside the machine.

The signature shows that this receipt was not changed after it was signed, and that one key signed it. The public key travels inside the receipt, so the signature does not show who held the key. Compare the key id with the key of the machine that issued it.
The receipt cannot be amended. A finding that appears after it was issued needs a new receipt, and the old one stays as it is.

Checks run on tool calls that reach the hooks. A shell command is read as text. A program that the job starts can do things the text does not show. Network use is checked by command names, tool names and a text scan of scripts. Personal data checks cover the paths named in the charter, with the patterns named there.
Staying on course means no unresolved pause and every stage reported done and passing its exit checks. It does not mean the result is right.

Result verified means each success criterion passed a check that failed on its planted fault. A check can pass its fault test and still miss a different fault. The comparison with the answer key is a second look, and it exists only when the operator supplied a key with a compare script.
The operator secret and the signing key are kept from the worker by Claude Code permission rules and the sandbox, not by the operating system.
Hook overhead has not been measured, and token counts are not recorded.
